aes: Spoken by all generations; parents pass it on to their children without interruption.
Most children speak it, but only in some areas of life – for example at home.
Children no longer learn it at home as their mother tongue.
Grandparents speak it. Parents understand it, but don't speak it to their children or among themselves.
The youngest speakers are grandparents and older – and they speak it only partly and rarely.
There are no living speakers left.
It has no native speakers any more, but people are learning it again and bringing it back to life. On the UNESCO scale it counts as extinct.

znakovyVysvetleni: A sign language is not spoken but shown – with the hands, facial expressions and body movement. It is used mainly by Deaf people and their families. It is not a spoken language translated into hands: it has its own words and its own grammar.
aesZnak: Deaf children pick it up naturally – from Deaf parents, at school and in the Deaf community.
Deaf children use it, but only in some places – for example only in some schools or towns.
Most Deaf children no longer learn it.
Mostly older Deaf people sign it; younger ones no longer pick it up.
Only a few elderly signers are left, and they rarely use it.
It has no native signers any more, but people are learning it again. On the UNESCO scale it counts as extinct.
